Order 
This appeal under Section 378(III) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed by the appellant/State assailing the judgment of acquittal dated 20.6.2011 passed in S.T.No. 140/2010,
whereby the learned 12th Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal, District Bhopoal (M.P.), whereby the respondents/accused, have been acquitted of the offence under Sections 379, 411, 420, 468, 471 of the IPC.
2.

entities.text: 12th Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal, District Bhopoal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Briefly stated, as per prosecution story, on 1.4.2009 at around 3:00 A.M., the appellants are alleged to have stolen a motorcycle bearing registration No. MP 04 MH 7758 belonging to Mohammad Asif from outside the house No.56, Fish Market, Itwara, Bhopal.
They are also accused of dishonestly receiving the stolen motorcycle and tampering with its engine and chasis numbers.
On 4.4.2009, FIR bearing Crime No.121/2009 was lodged in Police Station Taliya, which is Exhibit P/1.
After investigation, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18377 2 CRA-1132-2017 charge sheet was filed against the accused persons under Sections 379, 411, 420, 468, 471 of IPC.

Accused persons abjured their guilt and claimed to be tried.
4.

In order to bring home the charges, the prosecution has examined as many as 9 witnesses, namely Mohammad Arif (PW-1), Mohammad Saheb (PW-2), Mohd. Faizan (PW-3), R. K. Dubey (PW-4),
Naved (PW-5), Kalimuddin (PW-6), Saleem Khan (PW-7), S. M. Tripathi (PW-8) and V. K.
Soni(PW-9)
and placed Ex.P/1 to P/10 the documents on record.
In defence, the respondents/accused did not choose to examine any witness.

5 . After appreciating the evidence on record, the learned trial Court acquitted the accused persons of all the charges, holding that the prosecution failed to establish that the seized motorcycle was the same vehicle which had allegedly been stolen from the complainant.
Hence, this appeal.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/State submitted that the trial Court erred in acquitting the respondents despite sufficient material available on record.

It was contended that the FIR (Ex. P/1)
mentions the registration number, engine number and chassis number of the motorcycle.

The vehicle recovered at the instance of respondent Irfan had tampered numbers, which were later restored by the Forensic Science Laboratory and the FSL report (Ex. P/4) confirmed the identity of the vehicle.

It was thus argued that the prosecution had successfully proved that the seized motorcycle was the same stolen vehicle and therefore the acquittal recorded by the trial Court is erroneous and liable to be set aside..
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18377 3 CRA-1132-2017 7 .

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/accused supported the judgment of the trial Court and submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove that the seized motorcycle was the one stolen from the complainant.
It was argued that the engine number and chassis number of the seized motorcycle do not match with those mentioned in the registration certificate of the vehicle.
It was further submitted that the prosecution failed to exhibit the registration certificate of the motorcycle for the reasons best known to it.
In absence of the registration certificate being proved on record, the identity of the vehicle remains doubtful.
It was also contended that there is an unexplained delay of three days in lodging the FIR, which further casts doubt on the prosecution case.
8. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant/ State and perused the record meticulously.
9 . In the present case, the prosecution case rests primarily on the recovery of the motorcycle allegedly stolen from the complainant.
However, the prosecution has not placed the registration certificate of the motorcycle on record nor has it been duly proved during the trial.
In absence of the registration certificate, the prosecution has failed to establish the exact engine number and chassis number of the alleged stolen motorcycle.

10. Although the prosecution has relied upon the FSL report (Ex. P/4) to show that the erased numbers were restored, the foundational document establishing the original engine and chassis numbers of the vehicle has not been proved on record.

Consequently, it cannot be conclusively held NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18377 4 CRA-1132-2017 that the motorcycle recovered from the possession of the accused persons was the same vehicle that had been stolen from the complainant.
11. Complainant Mohammad Arif (P.W.1) has not deposed about the registration number, Engine No. and Chasis No. of the stolen motorcycle.

The Seizure memo (Exhibit P/6) only contains Engine No. and Chasis No. and unless and until such Engine No. and Chasis No. is established to be the Engine No. and Chasis No. of the stolen motorcycle, no conviction can be based upon it.
12. The identification panchnama (Exhibit P/3) has not been exhibited to complainant Mohd Arif (P.W.1) who has identified the motorcycle.
Why this Panchnama has not been exhibited during the examination of Mohd. Arif (P.W.1) is not answered by the prosecution.
Mohd. Arif (P.W.1) has not stated about the identification of the vehicle that he has correctly identified the vehicle.

In these circumstances, the statement of Mohd. Faizan (P.W.3) and Naved (P.W.5) who are the witnesses of The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Moh. Irphan on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63858972/

Naved (P.W.5) turned hostile and did not support this document.

13. As far as the seizure of stolen motor cycle from the possession of present respondents is concerned, the witnesses of such seizure and memorandum (Exhibit P5 and P/6), Kalimuddin (P.W.6) and Saleem Khan (P.W.7) have turned hostile and did not support these documents as well as the proceedings as purportedly conducted by the prosecution.

Though S. M. Tripathi (P.W.8) had supported these documents (Exhibit P/5 and P/6), he NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18377 5 CRA-1132-2017 deposed about the Bajaj Discover Motorcycle having Engine No. and Chasis No.ML M A J 20186 and DXEB J 20522 but FIR contains different Engine No. and Chasis No. so also FSL report (Exhibit P/4).

He also deposed that he at the instance of accused has seized the motorcycle from the house of Abrar but what information has been given by the accused has not been proved verbatim by this witness, Exhibit P/5 has not been satisfactorily proved.
14. Furthermore, the FIR was lodged after a delay of three days from the date of the alleged incident and no satisfactory explanation for such delay has been placed on record.
This circumstance also creates doubt regarding the prosecution version.
15. In view of the aforesaid deficiencies in the prosecution case, the learned trial Court was justified in extending the benefit of doubt to the accused persons.
The findings recorded by the trial Court are based on proper appreciation of the evidence and cannot be said to be perverse or contrary to law.
16. It is settled principle of law that if there two views are possible from the evidence, the view favourable to the accused will prevail.
Therefore, the learned trial Court has rightly adopted such view and acquitted the respondent/accused from the levelled charge.
No ground emerges to this Court warranting interference in the judgment of acquittal by the learned trial Court.

17. In the case of State of Gujarat v. Jayrajbhai Punjabhai Varu, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18377 6 CRA-1132-2017 (2016) 14 SCC 151 the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that prosecution has to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: It is also the rule of justice in criminal law that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in the case, one pointing to the guilt of the accused and the other towards his innocence, the view which is favourable to the accused should be adopted.

In case of Nikhil Chandra Mondal v. State of W.B.,
(2023) 6 SCC 605 Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that it is a settled principle of law that however strong a suspicion may be, it cannot take place of a proof beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: Unless finding of the trial Court is found to be perverse or illegal/impossible, it is not permissible for the appellate Court to interfere with the same.

18. Recently in case of Mallappa & others v. State of Karnataka, (2024) 3 SCC 544, the Hon'ble Apex Court has again summarized the principles while deciding the appeal against acquittal which are as follows :-

sentences.text: Our criminal jurisprudence is essentially based on the promise that no innocent shall be condemned as guilty.
All the safeguards and the jurisprudential values of criminal law, are intended to prevent any failure of justice.

Ex consequenti, in the light of the aforesaid discussion and the ratio of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in aforesaid cases, on careful analysis of the evidence, the observations made by the learned trial Court in the impugned judgment are not found to be faulty.
The learned trial Court on proper appreciation of evidence available on record has rightly acquitted the respondents/accused.
There is no ground for interference with the findings of the trial Court.
Therefore, while affirming the findings of acquittal of present respondents by trial Court, the appeal being bereft of merit is hereby dismissed.
